newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy plans railway and ENEL reforms.
newsitem.headline: Italy plans railway and ENEL reforms.

text.p: Italy is planning major reforms to its state-run railway company Ferrovie delle Stato and electrical utility group ENEL which could include splitting the groups up, Italian newspapers reported on Saturday.

Il Sole 24 Ore said prime minister Romana Prodi had issued a directive for a plan which could see the railway company split in two by the end of 1997 -- one managing the rail lines and infrastructure and the second the train and rolling stock.
But unions are unhappy with a further move to abolish free rail tickets for staff and their families, and have called for rail strikes on February 9 and February 16.

For ENEL, the government is looking to liberalise the electricity market. A plan was drawn up two years ago to seperate the group into three operating companies covering energy production, transmission and distribution but was never followed up.
The government is hoping to privatise ENEL later this year.

Now, a parliament commission headed by undersecretary at the industry ministry Umberto Carpi has put forward a plan to make ENEL into a holding company to control different operating companies within the whole ENEL group.
"ENEL cannot be privatized as it is. It cannot pass from a public monopoly to a private monopoly," Carpi was reported as saying in the Corriere Delle Sera newspaper.
